items.title: Apply the job deadline to OpenAI-compatible jobs, not only the claude CLI
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/index.ts:97-99` passes `config.jobTimeoutSec * 1000` to `runClaude` only. `runOpenAiCompatible(jobDir, prompt, provider, log, config.proxyUrl)` gets no deadline. In `worker/src/modelRunners/openAiCompatibleRunner.ts:9-14,121-138`, the loop allows `MAX_TURNS = 20` turns, each with a 300 s `AbortSignal.timeout`. A gpt/deepseek/qwen job can therefore hold the single-job worker for up to 100 minutes, even though the operator configured a shorter `jobTimeoutSec`. The worker handles one job at a time and the poll loop is blocked meanwhile, so queued jobs and chat turns wait.

## Proposed change
Add an optional `timeoutMs` parameter to `runOpenAiCompatible`. Compute a deadline at the start. Before each turn, fail with `Error("<model> job timed out after Ns")` if the deadline has passed. Make each fetch use `AbortSignal.any([AbortSignal.timeout(COMPLETION_TIMEOUT_MS), deadlineSignal])`, or clamp the per-request timeout to the remaining time. Pass `config.jobTimeoutSec * 1000` from `processJob`. Add a `.test.ts` next to the runner, with a stubbed `fetch` that never resolves and a tiny timeout.

## Acceptance criteria
- `runOpenAiCompatible` accepts a timeout and rejects with a clear timeout message once it elapses, including while a request is in flight.
- `processJob` passes the same `jobTimeoutSec` budget for both providers.
- Omitting the timeout keeps today's behavior.
- A new test covers both the in-flight and between-turn expiry cases.
- `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `worker/`.

items.title: Include the tail of model output in the 'Model run exited with code N' job failure
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/index.ts:101-103` turns a non-zero exit into `Model run exited with code ${result.exitCode}`. That string becomes the job's `errorMessage` via `updateStatus(..., 'failed', message)` (`index.ts:123-130`). `runClaude` (`worker/src/modelRunners/claudeRunner.ts:49-58`) keeps stdout in `output`, but stderr is only forwarded to `onOutput` and never stored in the result. The failure reason shown on the Worker page is therefore just an exit code. The real cause, such as an auth error, a rate limit or a bad model, is only in the streamed log, which is batched and best-effort (`index.ts:56-65`).

## Proposed change
1. In `runClaude`, also append stderr to the capped `output` buffer, using the same tail-truncation as stdout.
2. In `processJob`, build the error as `Model run exited with code N: <last ~500 chars of result.output, trimmed>`. Omit the suffix when the output is empty.
3. Extract the message building into a small pure helper and unit-test it. Add a `claudeRunner` test with a fake `claude` script on PATH that writes to stderr and exits 1.

## Acceptance criteria
- A failing run's `errorMessage` contains the final lines of stderr/stdout, truncated to a fixed maximum.
- Output on a successful run is unchanged apart from the extra stderr text in `result.output`.
- The helper is covered by a test for empty, short and over-long output.
- `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `worker/`.

items.title: Create the job temp dir inside processJob's try so a mkdir failure can't crash the worker
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/index.ts:43-44` runs `mkdirSync(config.workDir, ...)` and `mkdtempSync(...)` before the `try` that starts at line 74. If the work dir is unwritable or the disk is full, these throw out of `processJob`. The main loop (`index.ts:190-192`) does not catch that, and `main()` is launched with `void main()` (line 215). The result is an unhandled rejection that kills the process. The job stays `claimed` on bridge with no failure status, and the flush interval is not yet set up. Every other failure in this function is reported via `updateStatus(..., 'failed')`.

## Proposed change
Move directory creation inside the `try`. Declare `let jobDir: string | undefined` outside it, and in `finally` only `rmSync` when it is set. Then a creation failure is logged and reported as a failed job like any other error. Add a test in the existing worker test style, with `config.workDir` pointing at a path under a regular file and a fake client that records `updateStatus` calls.

## Acceptance criteria
- With an uncreatable `workDir`, `processJob` resolves and calls `updateStatus(job.id, 'failed', <message>)`.
- The temp dir is still removed on success and failure when it was created.
- No behavior change on the happy path.
- `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `worker/`.

items.title: Cap read_file output in the OpenAI-compatible agent so one big file can't blow the context
items.body:
## Problem
In `worker/src/modelRunners/openAiCompatibleRunner.ts:80-83`, the `read_file` tool returns the whole file. The full result is pushed into `messages` at line 175, and only the log line is cut to 200 characters (line 174). Parcels can hold large files or lockfiles. One `read_file` call can then exceed the model's context window, and every later turn re-sends it. The job fails with an opaque provider 400 (`openAiCompatibleRunner.ts:140-142`), or runs up cost until it does.

## Proposed change
Add a `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` constant, for example 50_000. When a `read_file` result is longer, return the first N characters plus a note such as `[truncated: file has X chars; N shown]`. Optionally allow an `offset` argument in the tool schema. Keep `write_file` and `list_files` unchanged. Add a unit test of `executeTool`, exporting it or testing through a stubbed `fetch`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A file larger than the cap yields a truncated result with an explicit truncation notice that includes the total size.
- Files at or under the cap are returned unchanged.
- A test covers both cases.
- `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass in `worker/`.
